units.t: Elements and Principles of Design Review

learn: Line, shape, form, value, colour, space and texture are the visual vocabulary of art.
Strong artists use elements intentionally, not by accident.
Analysing a famous work element by element trains your eye.
check: Which is an element of art?
lessons.try: Analyse a famous painting by listing how it uses each element.

learn: Balance, contrast, emphasis, movement, pattern, rhythm, proportion and unity are the principles.
Principles describe how elements are organised.
The best compositions combine several principles.
check: Which is a principle of design?
lessons.try: Create a design that shows three principles clearly.

learn: Every artwork is a series of decisions.
Ask: what do I want the viewer to notice first? How should their eye move?
Revise to strengthen your intentions.
check: An artwork is a series of...
Artists plan where the viewer's eye will...
lessons.try: Revise an old artwork to improve its focal point.

learn: Hold your pencil at arm's length to compare proportions.
Use one part of an object as a unit to measure others.
Check angles by holding your pencil vertical or horizontal.
check: Angles can be checked by holding your pencil...
lessons.try: Draw a chair using sighting and measuring.

learn: Begin with a gesture line showing the pose.
Build the figure with simple shapes, then refine.
Draw clothed models in short and long poses.
lessons.try: Do five two-minute and one twenty-minute figure drawings of a clothed friend.

learn: Rooms can be drawn from observation using perspective.
Find the eye level and vanishing points.
Include furniture, light and shadows.
check: The first step is finding the...
lessons.try: Draw a corner of your room in perspective.

learn: Strong drawings use the full range from white to black.
Squinting helps you see value shapes.
Lack of dark values makes drawings look flat.
check: Lack of darks makes a drawing look...
A full value range goes from...
lessons.try: Do a value study of a photograph using five values.

learn: Light creates highlight, mid-tone, core shadow, reflected light and cast shadow.
Cast shadows are darkest near the object.
One consistent light source makes forms convincing.
lessons.try: Shade an egg lit by a single lamp.

learn: Chiaroscuro means "light-dark": strong contrast that creates drama.
Caravaggio (1571-1610) used dramatic lighting in his paintings.
It focuses attention and creates mood.
lessons.try: Draw a still life lit dramatically from one side.

learn: One-point perspective uses one vanishing point for objects seen straight on.
Two-point uses two for objects seen at a corner.
All horizontal lines recede to vanishing points on the horizon.
check: A building seen at a corner uses...
A hallway seen straight on uses...
lessons.try: Draw a city street in two-point perspective.

learn: Three-point perspective adds a third vanishing point above or below.
It shows views looking up at skyscrapers or down from a height.
Vertical lines converge toward the third point.
check: Three-point perspective adds a vanishing point...
lessons.try: Draw a tall building looking up in three-point perspective.

learn: Foreshortening makes objects pointing toward the viewer look shorter.
An arm pointing at you appears compressed.
Andrea Mantegna's "Lamentation over the Dead Christ" (about 1480) is a famous example.
check: A famous early foreshortening example is by...
lessons.try: Draw your hand pointing toward you.

learn: Complementary, analogous, triadic and split-complementary are colour schemes.
Triadic colours are evenly spaced: red, yellow, blue.
Simultaneous contrast: colours look different depending on neighbours.
check: Red, yellow, blue is a ___ scheme.
lessons.try: Paint the same grey square on red and on green; compare.

learn: Tints add white; shades add black; tones add grey.
Mixing complements makes neutral browns and greys.
Many painters mix shadows with a complement instead of black.
lessons.try: Paint a value scale for one hue using tints and shades.

lessons.t: Painting a Still Life in Colour
learn: Block in large colour shapes first.
Work from dark to light in opaque paint, or light to dark in watercolour.
Observe colour temperature: warm light, cool shadows.
lessons.try: Paint a still life with three objects.

learn: Relief prints ink the raised surface; carved areas stay white.
Linocut and woodcut are relief methods.
Use safe cutting tools, always cutting away from your hand, with a bench hook.
check: In relief printing, carved areas print...
lessons.try: Design a linocut and plan which areas will be carved.

learn: A reduction print carves and prints the same block in stages, lightest colour first.
Each stage removes more of the block.
Registration lines up the paper for each colour.
check: Reduction prints start with the ___ colour.
Lining up paper for each colour is...
Each stage of a reduction print removes...
lessons.try: Plan a three-colour reduction print.

learn: Intaglio prints from ink held in incised lines, as in etchings by Rembrandt.
Screen printing pushes ink through a stencil on mesh, used for posters and T-shirts.
Each method creates a distinct look.
check: Ink held in incised lines is...
lessons.try: Make a simple stencil and print it.

learn: Additive sculpture builds up material: clay, wire, cardboard.
Subtractive sculpture carves away: stone, wood, soap.
Plan from several views: front, side, top.
lessons.try: Carve a small sculpture from a bar of soap.

learn: An armature is an internal support, like a wire skeleton for a clay figure.
Structures must balance and support their weight.
Engineers and sculptors share ideas about load and stability.
lessons.try: Build a wire armature for a small figure.

learn: Industrial design shapes everyday objects: chairs, lamps, phones.
Form follows function: the design should suit the use.
Prototypes test ideas before final production.
check: "Form follows function" means design should suit the...
lessons.try: Design and prototype a cardboard phone stand.

learn: Cave paintings at Lascaux are about 17,000 years old.
Greek and Roman sculpture idealised the human form.
Medieval illuminated manuscripts decorated texts with gold and colour.
check: Lascaux paintings are about ___ years old.
lessons.try: Design an illuminated first letter of your name.

lessons.t: Art of Asia, Africa and the Americas
learn: Chinese scroll paintings show landscapes meant to be unrolled slowly.
Benin bronzes from West Africa record royal history.
Mesoamerican artists created codices and carved stone monuments.
lessons.try: Compare a Chinese scroll and a European landscape painting.

learn: Modern art (about 1860-1970) broke with tradition: Impressionism, Cubism, Abstract Expressionism.
Contemporary art (since about 1970) includes installation, video and digital art.
Contemporary artists often explore identity, technology and society.
lessons.try: Research a contemporary art form and present it.

learn: Raster images are made of pixels and lose quality when enlarged.
Vector images use mathematical paths and stay sharp at any size.
Logos are usually vectors; photographs are rasters.
lessons.try: Zoom in on a raster and a vector image and compare.

learn: Digital painting uses brushes, layers and undo.
Layers let you edit parts separately.
Many digital skills mirror traditional ones: value, colour and composition.
lessons.try: Make a digital painting with at least three layers.

learn: Design posters, album covers and book jackets with hierarchy, alignment and contrast.
Use a grid to align elements.
White space gives designs room to breathe.
lessons.try: Design a book cover for a public-domain novel.

learn: Describe, analyse, interpret and judge.
Support every judgment with evidence from the artwork.
Consider the artist's intent and the context.
check: The time and place of the work
lessons.try: Write a formal critique of a classmate's work.

learn: A portfolio shows your best and most varied work.
Include sketches to show process.
Arrange works so they tell a story of your growth.
lessons.try: Select ten works for your portfolio.

learn: Exhibitions present art to an audience with labels and artist statements.
Lighting and spacing affect how work is seen.
Reflect on audience responses.
lessons.try: Plan a small class exhibition.
